status: None of these sources supplies the requested universal upper bound or a proved transfer to it.
source_policy: Technical conclusions below are based on primary papers, not search-result summaries alone.

entries.title: Betti numbers of semi-algebraic sets defined by multi-degree constraints
entries.authors: Saugata Basu and Anthony Rizzie
entries.checked_location: Theorems 12 and 13, printed page 11; general multi-block formulas in Notation 3 and Theorems 12-13, printed page 11, for dyadic weighted-degree groups
entries.mechanism: Bounds on components of sign conditions using separate parameter blocks and their separate degrees.
entries.application: The two-block estimate in mechanism-audit.tex gives a full-model lower bound with asymptotic constant one. It also excludes low-rank denominator directions, adaptive moment-curve nodes, and uniformly mild conditioning/margin as universal compressed constructions.
entries.gap: A sign-pattern upper count is a lower-bound method for head complexity. It provides no universal existence construction.
entries.application_all_order_jets: The explicit dependence on the number of blocks is only a polynomial raised to the parameter dimension. Dyadic order grouping bounds arbitrary-order Taylor clusters; polynomially many adaptive bases remain non-universal at the target budget.

entries.title: The capacity of feedforward neural networks
entries.authors: Pierre Baldi and Roman Vershynin
entries.checked_location: Theorem 3.1 and its dimensional assumptions
entries.mechanism: Capacity estimates for layered threshold networks.
entries.gap: The dimensional hypotheses used for the relevant asymptotics do not cover exponentially many hidden units relative to input dimension. Counting many functions is also weaker than representing every function, and a threshold activation is not an admissible head value.

entries.title: Exact hyperplane covers for subsets of the hypercube
entries.authors: James Aaronson, Carla Groenland, Andrzej Grzesik, Tom Johnston, and Bartłomiej Kielak
entries.checked_location: Theorem 2, Lemmas 9 and 10, and their proofs
entries.mechanism: Hamming-neighborhood covers and a count of hyperplane intersection patterns.
entries.gap: The universal upper bound has order 2^n/n. The lower bound has order 2^n/n^2. Moreover a hyperplane equality predicate cannot simply be inserted as a flat-valued head and combined by an assumed free OR operation.

entries.title: Explicit exponential lower bounds for exact hyperplane covers
entries.authors: Benjamin E. Diamond and Amir Yehudayoff
entries.checked_location: Introduction and main lower-bound theorem
entries.mechanism: Communication complexity gives explicit subsets with exponentially large exact cover number.
entries.gap: This is a lower bound for a different covering resource, not a universal construction at the requested scale.

entries.title: Dimension of projections in Boolean functions
entries.authors: Ramamohan Paturi and Francis Zane
entries.checked_location: Theorem 2 and definition of a projection
entries.mechanism: Find monochromatic projections defined by fixed coordinates and equal or complementary coordinate identifications.
entries.gap: The guaranteed dimension is around log_2(n), not 2 log_2(n). This does not provide arbitrary-label cells of quadratic size or an admissible-head compiler.

entries.title: Stability for hyperplane covers
entries.authors: Shagnik Das, Valjakas Djaljapayan, Yen-Chi Roger Lin, Wei-Hsuan Yu
entries.checked_location: Weighted hyperplane inequality and its equality and stability conditions
entries.mechanism: The vertex weight 1/(|x| binomial(n,|x|)) bounds the weight of a hyperplane avoiding the origin.
entries.gap: Almost covers and multiplicity covers do not supply target-dependent monochromatic exact covers of arbitrary subsets. No head-count upper bound follows.

entries.title: Polynomial threshold functions and Boolean threshold circuits
entries.authors: Kristoffer Arnsfelt Hansen and Vladimir V. Podolskii
entries.checked_location: Section 5, especially Lemmas 19 and 20
entries.mechanism: Compare maxima of affine input statistics, then lift a strict exponent winner to a signed exponential sum.
entries.gap: An exponential of an affine input statistic is a product over input coordinates. It is not an affine numerator or denominator. The dominant-power head construction instead takes maxima over active coefficient exponents and has a different feasibility problem.

entries.title: Sign conditions for injectivity of generalized polynomial maps with applications to chemical reaction networks and real algebraic geometry
entries.authors: Stefan Mueller, Elisenda Feliu, Georg Regensburger, Carsten Conradi, Anne Shiu, Alicia Dickenstein
entries.checked_location: Theorems 1.4 and 1.5, especially the existence clause of Theorem 1.5
entries.mechanism: Oriented-matroid conditions on maximal minors give injectivity and, with additional hypotheses, positive solutions in a specified cone.
entries.gap: Arbitrary Boolean label cones do not automatically satisfy the required matching-minor signs. Establishing the relevant compatibility at the requested head count remains a theorem-strength gap.

entries.title: Unit signatures in real biquadratic and multiquadratic number fields
entries.authors: David S. Dummit and Hershy Kisilevsky
entries.checked_location: Definitions of signature and deficiency, Proposition 1, and the introductory statements of the main constructions
entries.mechanism: Real embeddings of a multiquadratic field are indexed by Boolean sign choices, so algebraic signatures form Boolean tables.
entries.gap: The constructions concern multiplicative unit groups and extraction of square roots. These operations have no established small-head compilation. Signature rank can also be deficient; unrestricted signature universality must not be assumed for units.
entries.implementation_audit: A product of admissible denominators is strictly log-submodular on every coordinate square if any denominator is nonconstant. Therefore a norm-one table cannot be factored into nonconstant admissible affine conjugates. This excludes that fixed-norm implementation, not all uses of arithmetic signatures.

entries.title: Erzeugungsgrad, VC-dimension and neural networks with rational activation function
entries.authors: Luis Miguel Pardo and Daniel Sebastian
entries.checked_location: Introduction; Section 5.5, especially Lemma 5.12, Corollary 5.13 and Definition 25 (rechecked in the HTML version).
entries.mechanism: Intersection theory bounds the growth function of classifiers given by distinguished Zariski-open sets D(f/g)={x:f(x)g(x)!=0} over an algebraically closed field; it also bounds the size and density of identity-testing sequences.
entries.gap: These classifiers test nonvanishing, not the positive versus negative real sign required here. The results give upper growth bounds and identity tests, not shattering of the fixed Boolean cube or a construction with positive same-sign-slope affine denominators.
entries.rechecked_2026_11_23: Re-read the stated model distinctions and principal bounds; no stronger transfer found.

entries.title: Network size and weights size for memorization with two-layers neural networks
entries.authors: Sebastien Bubeck, Ronen Eldan, Yin Tat Lee, Dan Mikulincer
entries.checked_location: Introduction, general-position condition, and stated memorization bounds
entries.mechanism: Threshold and ReLU memorization at the number-of-points divided by input-dimension scale; complex recombination controls weights in approximation.
entries.gap: The scale is 2^n/n, the cube fails the stated general-position condition, and the activations differ from admissible affine ratios.

entries.title: The real tropical geometry of neural networks
entries.authors: Marie-Charlotte Brandenburg, Georg Loho, Guido Montufar
entries.checked_location: Classification regions and the distinction between real and tropical parameter geometry
entries.mechanism: Tropical inequalities organize classification regions and reveal nonconvexity.
entries.gap: The geometry alone does not assert a solution for every labeling or provide positive affine denominators with the required head count.

entries.title: Neural Nets with Superlinear VC-Dimension
entries.authors: Wolfgang Maass
entries.checked_location: Permutation encoding construction and its two hidden layers
entries.mechanism: A small collection of permutations encodes arbitrary bit tables on specially chosen one-hot input triples.
entries.gap: The decoding uses exclusive OR and additional threshold processing. The positive-denominator decoder in mechanism-audit.tex establishes only promised-grid permutation decoding; it does not compile the extra nonlinear operations or cover the full cube.

entries.title: Counting and Covering in Nearest-Neighbour Representations of Boolean Functions
entries.authors: Martin Anthony
entries.checked_location: Introduction and Section 3 counting and VC-dimension estimates
entries.mechanism: Counting prototype systems and comparison with unions of halfspaces.
entries.gap: The full-cube universal upper bound described in the paper remains at order 2^n/n. A matching capacity order on some point set is not shattering of the fixed Boolean cube, and nearest-neighbour evaluation is not an affine-ratio score.

entries.title: VC Dimension and Expressivity of Real-Valued Transformers
entries.authors: Gavin Dooley, Andy Yang, Yijia Jessica Zhu, David Chiang, Peter Cholak, Anand Pillay
entries.checked_location: Architecture-dependent VC statements and Proposition 6.3 indexing construction
entries.mechanism: Definability bounds and a one-layer indexing example.
entries.gap: The indexing query contains the requested index k. The manuscript fixes the query token, so that example is not a decoder in the present model. Architecture-dependent VC bounds also do not give the requested universal head-count construction.

entries.title: Geometric complexity theory for product-plus-power
entries.authors: Pranjal Dutta, Fulvio Gesmundo, Christian Ikenmeyer, Gorav Jindal, Vladimir Lysikov
entries.checked_location: Introduction, Theorem 1.1, and the Newton-identity argument
entries.mechanism: Relates border product-plus-power complexity to border Waring rank over the complex numbers.
entries.gap: Complex roots-of-unity cancellation has no established real positive-affine-denominator compiler. The elementary second-order real cancellation obstruction is recorded separately in mechanism-audit.tex.

entries.title: Extremal properties of polynomial threshold functions
entries.authors: Ryan O’Donnell and Rocco A. Servedio
entries.checked_location: Definitions 1 and 2, Theorem 3, and Section 6.1 proofs of Theorems 13 and 14
entries.mechanism: Weak polynomial sign representations supported on a monochromatic restriction or affine subspace.
entries.gap: Weak representations may vanish at most inputs, whereas the requested representation must have a strict sign everywhere. Polynomial products and parity constraints also lack a proved small-head compiler.
entries.revisit: Table 2 and Section 5 distinguish strong PTF density from weak density; the strong-density lower bound is a positive constant times 2^n. A universal order-2^n/n Fourier-monomial support would contradict that bound.

entries.title: Algebraic aspects of discrete tomography
entries.authors: Lajos Hajdu and Robert Tijdeman
entries.checked_location: Theorem 1, the divisibility lemma, and their proofs on pages 5-7
entries.mechanism: Functions with zero line sums on an integer rectangle are generated by translates of a product of binomials for the projection directions.
entries.gap: These are cancellation identities, not strict-sign interpolation of arbitrary Boolean labels. Neither a small support with the necessary directions nor a universal admissible-head perturbation follows from the theorem.
entries.revisit: Checked Theorem 1 and Corollary 1 again for affine permutation-valued cubes. Projection invariance does not compile permutation signs into allowed fraction sums.
entries.revisit_2026_11_23: The coefficient-space version is now proved directly in toric-switching-audit.tex: an exact complete-intersection kernel and subset-difference divisibility characterize all Boolean projections. No sparse-support bound is obtained.

entries.title: Orthogonal Vector-Valued Rational Functions with Applications in Rational Approximation
entries.authors: Robbe Vermeiren
entries.checked_location: Introduction, Definition 2.1, Definition 2.3, and Problem 2.4
entries.mechanism: Construct orthonormal bases with prescribed poles and prescribed residue directions, including an inverse-eigenvalue formulation and tangential rational Krylov algorithms.
entries.application: Informs numerical conditioning audits of the Cauchy codebook experiment.
entries.gap: The paper fixes pole and direction data and assumes a nondegenerate discrete inner product. It does not assert arbitrary strict-sign realizability by target-dependent positive shifts.

entries.title: Almost every Boolean function has central threshold degree
entries.authors: Martin Anthony
entries.checked_location: Theorem 1 and the proof of Lemma 2
entries.mechanism: Relate the fraction of polynomial sign patterns to real evaluation ranks and then to Reed-Muller erasure recovery over the binary field.
entries.gap: The theorem concerns almost all functions and polynomial degree. It supplies neither every-function coverage nor a compiler into the admissible affine-fraction model at the requested head count.

entries.title: Old and new examples of k-nets in P^2
entries.authors: Janis Stipins
entries.checked_location: Definition 1.1, Propositions 2.2 and 2.10, and Sections 4.2-4.5
entries.mechanism: Products of line equations in a pencil, including constructions from finite elliptic-curve subgroups and explicit real low-degree nets.
entries.gap: Incidence and factorization identities do not supply arbitrary Boolean signs or Boolean-compatible affine embeddings. Some configurations, including the displayed Hesse four-net, are intrinsically complex.

entries.title: Completely reducible hypersurfaces in a pencil
entries.authors: J. V. Pereira and S. Yuzvinsky
entries.checked_location: Theorem 2.1, its stated irreducible-generic-fiber hypothesis, and Section 6.2
entries.mechanism: Bound the essential dimension of pencils with several completely split fibers and give reflection-group examples of product identities.
entries.gap: Theorems concern full polynomial identities over the complex field. They cannot be applied directly to identities modulo the Boolean ideal, nor without checking the generic-fiber hypothesis. No arbitrary-sign head construction follows.

entries.title: Small Boolean Sections in Alon-Furedi Covers
entries.authors: Zoltan Lorant Nagy
entries.checked_location: Theorems 1.3 and 3.2, Proposition 3.3, and the complete control-slice proof in Section 3
entries.mechanism: Explicit integer hyperplanes permute Hamming layers between binary control slices; a roots-of-unity estimate balances their intersection sizes at (1+o(1))*2^n/n.
entries.gap: This is a balanced cover of all vertices except one. It is not a cover of an arbitrary target-dependent subset, and no additive implementation of its product polynomial by the requested number of admissible heads is supplied.

entries.title: Understanding the Loss Surface of Neural Networks for Binary Classification
entries.authors: Shiyu Liang, Ruoyu Sun, Yixuan Li, R. Srikant
entries.checked_location: Theorems 1 and 2 and their data assumptions
entries.mechanism: Exclude bad local minima under label-dependent subspace separation or linear separability assumptions, with suitable smooth activations and losses.
entries.gap: Arbitrary Boolean labelings do not satisfy these assumptions. The theorem does not prove attainment or a zero-loss configuration for the requested rational model.

entries.title: Spurious Valleys in One-hidden-layer Neural Network Optimization Landscapes
entries.authors: Luca Venturi, Afonso S. Bandeira, Joan Bruna
entries.checked_location: Theorem 8 and its proof in Appendix A.1
entries.mechanism: At width at least the upper intrinsic dimension, redundant units can be exchanged until the feature matrix spans the relevant space, after which the readout is optimized convexly.
entries.gap: The width condition uses the dimension of the full feature span. It does not provide every-label sign coverage with width smaller by the requested factor.

entries.title: The smallest sets of points not determined by their X-rays
entries.authors: Andreas Alpers and David G. Larman
entries.checked_location: Theorems 2.1, 2.2, 3.3 and the complete pigeonhole proof in Section 3
entries.mechanism: Choose many short primitive lattice directions; count projection data of half-sized subsets of a lattice box to produce two distinct subsets with equal projections and polynomial support size.
entries.gap: The directions are selected as part of the construction. The result does not provide polynomial-size unweighted switching components for prescribed directions, arbitrary Boolean sign tables, or an admissible-head compiler at the target count.

entries.title: On the reconstruction of static and dynamic discrete structures
entries.authors: Andreas Alpers and Peter Gritzmann
entries.checked_location: Theorems 3-5 and Section 8, especially Theorems 24 and 25
entries.mechanism: Switching components in several directions yield multivariate equal-power-sum identities and Prouhet-Tarry-Escott solutions.
entries.gap: Equal moments are cancellation constraints. They do not by themselves interpolate arbitrary strict signs, and the planar direction-selection hypothesis is not a Boolean-cube embedding theorem.

entries.title: Two applications of number theory to discrete tomography
entries.authors: Rob Tijdeman
entries.checked_location: Sections 2-4, including the direct substitution proof of Theorem 3.2
entries.mechanism: Encode weighted point sets by bivariate polynomials; zero line sums imply divisibility by direction binomials, hence by their product in a unique factorization domain.
entries.gap: This gives switching identities rather than arbitrary sign interpolation. The general Chinese-remainder assertion as printed in Theorem 3.1 must not be used without a comaximality hypothesis: the coprime polynomials x,y with remainders 0,1 are already incompatible at (0,0). The product-divisibility implication used here is valid independently of that assertion.

entries.title: Light RUMs
entries.authors: Flavio Chierichetti, Ravi Kumar, Andrew Tomkins
entries.checked_location: Theorem 1, Observation 8, Corollary 9, Theorems 10 and 12
entries.mechanism: Sampling gives O(n/epsilon^2) permutations or multinomial-logit components with uniform additive approximation over all slates.
entries.gap: A Boolean sign transfer needs quantitative margins. The exact outside-option choice polytope has maximum axis-parallel cube radius 1/(3^n-1); the fixed-center uniform-perturbation transfer therefore gives no target bound. Arbitrary signed affine payoffs remain outside this obstruction.

entries.title: The VC Dimension and Pseudodimension of Two-Layer Neural Networks with Discrete Inputs
entries.authors: Peter L. Bartlett and Robert C. Williamson
entries.checked_location: Publisher abstract; complete searchable textbook PDF, Anthony and Bartlett Theorem 8.11 and proof on printed pages 122-123, inspected separately on 2026-11-21.
entries.mechanism: Transforms sigmoid outputs on discrete inputs into rational functions and bounds sign patterns. The original abstract reports O(W log(WD)).
entries.gap: The original abstract gives O(W log(WD)). The textbook PDF extraction asserts degree 3ND+2 after combining k rational outputs. Independent partial fractions force degree at least k-1 in general, so this head-independent clearing step cannot be transferred. Screenshot calls returned no viewable image and a local download failed DNS; the textbook theorem itself is not declared false.

entries.title: Nearest neighbor representations of Boolean functions
entries.authors: Peter Hajnal, Zhihao Liu, Gyorgy Turan
entries.checked_location: Sections 5 and 8; universal bound and discussion of the threshold-circuit gap
entries.mechanism: Covers the Boolean cube by radius-one neighborhoods and uses geometric prototypes to represent local labels.
entries.gap: The universal bound has order 2^n/n. Nearest-prototype comparisons are not affine fractions with the manuscript's coefficient restrictions, and the paper does not supply a sharper universal construction.

entries.title: Provable Tempered Overfitting of Minimal Nets and Typical Nets
entries.authors: Itamar Harel, William M. Hoza, Gal Vardi, Itay Evron, Nathan Srebro, Daniel Soudry
entries.checked_location: Theorem 3.1; Appendix D, especially the hitting-set generator outline and finite-field generator construction
entries.mechanism: Uses hitting-set generators and finite-field independence to encode arbitrary partial Boolean tables with nearly optimal binary description length.
entries.gap: The construction uses a depth-14 threshold network. No one-layer affine-fraction compilation preserving the required head count is established.

entries.title: Betweenness and Nonbetweenness
entries.authors: Ross Atkins
entries.checked_location: Theorem 1.5 and Lemmas 3.1 and 3.2
entries.mechanism: Constructs a logarithmic number of permutations that between-satisfy every ternary constraint, using separating orders and half-order rotations.
entries.gap: Ternary betweenness coverage is distinct from a large disjoint matching in every prescribed orthant. The deterministic rank-distance argument in the audit excludes the earlier full-rate matching criterion even for structured dictionaries.

entries.title: Neural Networks with Quadratic VC Dimension
entries.authors: Pascal Koiran and Eduardo D. Sontag
entries.checked_location: Proposition 1, Theorems 2, 4, and 6, Lemmas 1 and 2
entries.mechanism: Whole Boolean-cube shattering through scalar memory lookup and sequential bit extraction; an arithmetic variant uses iterates of the logistic map.
entries.gap: The construction uses depth, intermediate multiplication, and interpolation. It does not supply a one-layer sum of admissible affine fractions, and flattening with the requested head count has not been proved.

entries.title: MultivariateApart: Generalized Partial Fractions
entries.authors: Matthias Heller and Andreas von Manteuffel
entries.checked_location: Section 2.1, Definition 1 and Algorithm 1 in Section 2.2
entries.mechanism: Leinartas decomposition separates denominator factors with no common zero or algebraic dependence.
entries.gap: Terms retain products of up to the number of variables in algebraically independent denominator factors. Iterated univariate partial fractions can introduce extra poles. Neither operation gives affine numerators over single admissible affine denominators.

entries.title: Extremal and approximative properties of simple partial fractions
entries.authors: V. I. Danchenko, M. A. Komarov and P. V. Chunaev
entries.checked_location: Definition (1), Sections 6.1 and 6.2
entries.mechanism: Interpolation by logarithmic derivatives of complex univariate polynomials; reduction to polynomial interpolation.
entries.gap: The model permits complex poles and concerns univariate interpolation. The universal simple-node result uses degree at least twice the number of nodes minus one, and does not provide constrained multivariate Boolean sign compression.

entries.title: On Explicit Super-Expressive Approximation for Neural Networks
entries.authors: Feng-Lei Fan, Ze-Yu Li, Chen-Yu Wang and Jian-Jun Wang
entries.checked_location: Definitions 5-7; Section 3.1; Lemmas 8 and 9; equations (19)-(23)
entries.mechanism: Pairwise coprime affine moduli 1+i c with factorial c encode arbitrary quantized labels by the Chinese Remainder Theorem.
entries.gap: The decoder explicitly applies floor after a reciprocal and multiplies two hidden-channel values. These operations and the five-layer architecture are absent from the stipulated affine-fraction sum. A low-head compiler has not been established.

entries.title: Algebraic Geometry of Rational Neural Networks
entries.authors: Alexandros Grosdos, Elina Robeva and Maksym Zubkov
entries.checked_location: Section 4.3, Lemma 4.9; Proposition 4.4
entries.mechanism: Relates reciprocal-network numerators to projections of Chow varieties by expanding a product of affine forms with auxiliary variables.
entries.gap: Complex Zariski closures and exact rational-function parameterizations do not establish strict Boolean sign coverage with positive same-sign-slope denominators.

entries.title: New Gate, Weight and Wire Complexity Bounds for Sigmoid Neural Networks
entries.authors: Jiatu Li, Daniel Reichman, Ryan Williams and Tony Wu
entries.checked_location: Theorems 1.1-1.9; Section 4.2; Section 6.3; detailed rereading: Theorem 6.1, Lemma 6.6, Corollary 6.7, Lemma 6.8, Corollary 6.9, proof of Theorem 1.7 in Section 6.3, and statement of Lemma 7.1; Theorem 4.4 and Lemma 4.5; Appendix B.3, Proposition B.4 and proof (HTML reread)
entries.mechanism: Rational approximation, algebraic parameter bounds, and sequential bit extraction give bounds and simulations for sigmoid circuits. Approximate multiplication through second differences, carry-free packed products, and sequential bit decoding give a small circuit for inner product modulo two.
entries.gap: The decoder uses growing depth. A sigmoid denominator on Boolean inputs is 1+B*product_j(W_j^x_j), which is not an affine input denominator. Parameter compression preserves a pre-existing circuit and does not reduce gate count. The construction does not transfer to the manuscript model or prove the universal bound.
entries.rational_approximation_gap: A rational approximant with no pole on an interval can have higher-degree or non-real-pole denominator; neither property supplies a same-cost sum of admissible affine fractions.

entries.title: Boolean threshold functions, neuron capacity, and memory retrieval
entries.authors: Xinyuan Xie
entries.checked_location: Theorem 1, Corollary 2, Theorem 3, and the chamber-count argument in Section 2.1
entries.mechanism: Sharp asymptotic enumeration of linear threshold functions, via random sign-vector spans and hyperplane-arrangement chambers.
entries.gap: Counting about 2^(n^2) single-neuron functions does not prove that O(2^n/n^2) neurons cover every Boolean labeling. This paper supplies neither an admissible affine-ratio decoder nor the required universal covering theorem.

entries.title: On Non-Deterministic Representation of Boolean Functions
entries.authors: Sudharshan Rajagopalan and Nitin Saurabh
entries.checked_location: Theorem 3, Lemma 4, Theorems 6-8, Proposition 26 and Lemma 27; matrix Chernoff estimate (5) in the proof of Theorem 3 and Corollary 5
entries.mechanism: A random Hadamard submatrix has full row rank after deletion of any column, giving almost-all nondeterministic and rational degree n/2+O(sqrt(n log n)). The paper also gives five affine forms for which a compatible Boolean partition of unity must have unbounded degree.
entries.gap: The degree theorem concerns a negligible exceptional fraction, not every function, and its polynomial numerator and denominator are not an affine-fraction head decomposition. The displayed probability estimate is not an exponentially small fraction in the truth-table length, so fixed-codimension extension does not promote it to a worst-case bound.

entries.title: Concerning synthesis of depth two schemes of step elements
entries.authors: N. P. Red'kin
entries.checked_location: Definitions and main theorem on printed pages 82-84; spherical decomposition in Lemma 1
entries.mechanism: Partition a power-of-two-dimensional cube into open Hamming neighborhoods. A threshold gate handles an arbitrary labeling of each neighborhood and its center, then auxiliary gates correct center values.
entries.gap: The stated Shannon complexity is the sum of absolute integer input weights, not gate count. The construction uses cells of linear size. Threshold outputs are not affine-fraction head values, so neither the desired quadratic saving nor an admissible compiler follows.

entries.title: Balanced Gray Codes
entries.authors: Girish S. Bhat and Carla D. Savage
entries.checked_location: Lemma 2 and Theorem 1, including the explicit transition-count selection proof
entries.mechanism: A Gray enumeration in every dimension with each bit changing within two of the average number of transitions.
entries.gap: It gives efficient separate scalar polynomials for one-hot bit addresses. Binary addressing and a full-cube encoder do not follow from this theorem.

entries.title: Near Optimal Single-Track Gray Codes
entries.authors: Tuvi Etzion and Kenneth G. Paterson
entries.checked_location: Example 4, properties C1-C3, Lemma 19, and Theorems 20-21
entries.mechanism: Order all self-dual necklaces in power-of-two word lengths with neighboring representatives at Hamming distance two. A modified full enumeration has one generating track with few transitions, enabling the explicit binary-addressed affine-fraction scalar decoder proved in mechanism-audit.tex.
entries.gap: The code parameter remains an independent positive scalar. Supplying arbitrary codewords at all cube inputs, and composing or aggregating such encoders without extra head cost, remains unproved.

entries.title: The structure of single-track Gray codes
entries.authors: Moshe Schwartz and Tuvi Etzion
entries.checked_location: Definitions 3-5 and Theorems 1-4, including the self-dual construction and equally spaced reading positions
entries.mechanism: Describes cyclic column shifts and the relation to full-order self-dual necklaces; separates full enumerations from the stricter Gray adjacency condition.
entries.gap: The binary full-period Gray obstruction does not prohibit our enumeration, which permits several bits to change at block boundaries. Neither type of enumeration supplies the missing full-cube encoder.

entries.title: Asymmetric Binary Covering Codes
entries.authors: Joshua N. Cooper, Robert B. Ellis, Andrew B. Kahng
entries.checked_location: Propositions 6 and 7, Corollary 8, Theorem 9, printed pages 237-240
entries.mechanism: Patched covers and a semidirect sum give downward radius-R covers of size O_R(2^n/n^R) for every dimension.
entries.application: Radius one gives the explicit positive-slope Mobius-basis initialization in mechanism-audit.tex.
entries.gap: Radius two provides the desired number of cells but requires quadratic local numerators. A constant-head compiler for arbitrary labels on one radius-two ball is excluded by a local Warren count. No global interacting replacement is established.

entries.title: The Entropic Discriminant
entries.authors: Raman Sanyal, Bernd Sturmfels, Cynthia Vinzant
entries.checked_location: Introduction, equations (1)-(2), and the real analytic-center description
entries.mechanism: Reciprocal row-space equations describe analytic centers, one for each bounded region of an affine coordinate-hyperplane arrangement. Generic solutions are all real.
entries.gap: Realness of these particular intersections does not guarantee arbitrary signs in a sum of admissible affine fractions. Positivity selects a particular branch. No bound on the required number of summands follows.

entries.title: The Chow form of a reciprocal linear space
entries.authors: Mario Kummer and Cynthia Vinzant
entries.checked_location: Definition 1.1, Propositions 1.3-1.4, Definition 5.1, Theorem 5.2 and Lemma 5.3
entries.mechanism: Hyperbolicity under coordinatewise inversion and explicit determinantal equations for reciprocal-space intersections and Hadamard products.
entries.gap: The all-real intersections use prescribed complementary linear spaces. The Hadamard-product theorem is over generic complex linear spaces and concerns a defining equation, not every real orthant or a positive denominator branch. A universal low-head sign-covering assertion remains unproved.

entries.title: Which n-Venn diagrams can be drawn with convex k-gons?
entries.authors: Jeremy Carroll, Frank Ruskey, Mark Weston
entries.checked_location: Theorem 2.3, Table 1, and Section 5
entries.mechanism: Counts intersections of convex polygon curves and constructs a sharp seven-curve example.
entries.gap: The order 2^n/n^2 expression in Theorem 2.3 is a lower bound on polygon sides. It is not a general construction. Polygon membership predicates and arbitrary planar code locations have no supplied affine-fraction compiler or cube encoder.

entries.title: The Z4-Linearity of Kerdock, Preparata, Goethals and Related Codes
entries.authors: A. Roger Hammons Jr., P. Vijay Kumar, A. R. Calderbank, N. J. A. Sloane, Patrick Sole
entries.checked_location: Theorems 13-15 and Section 5.3
entries.mechanism: Quaternary linear duality explains the weight distributions. For binary length l=2^(m+1), odd m>=3, the Preparata image has 2^l/l^2 codewords, minimum distance six, and covering radius at most four via the Gray isometry.
entries.gap: The count is a code size, not a representation of arbitrary labels. The finite-ring syndrome decoder uses operations not supplied by a one-layer affine-ratio score. Global cancellation across cells and an admissible low-head decoder are not proved.

entries.title: The Quarks of Attention: Structure and Capacity of Neural Attention Building Blocks
entries.authors: Pierre Baldi and Roman Vershynin
entries.checked_location: Sections 4.3, 5.5, and Theorem 7.1 with its proof
entries.mechanism: Threshold-unit gating and selector multiplexing yield cardinal-capacity estimates. Theorem 7.1 gives capacity asymptotic to 2mn^2 for m<=2^{o(n)}.
entries.gap: This counts a family of Boolean functions; it does not assert every truth table is represented. The required width is outside the stated subexponential regime. Threshold gating and its iterated products are not the manuscript affine-fraction score operations.

entries.title: Rational Neural Networks have Expressivity Advantages
entries.authors: Maosen Tang and Alex Townsend
entries.checked_location: Version 2, Section 3 and Theorems 4.1-4.4
entries.mechanism: Low-degree rational gates achieve high-degree rational approximation by composition across depth.
entries.gap: The size savings depend on depth and rational denominators of degree greater than one. No flattening theorem into the manuscript one-layer affine-ratio family, or all-Boolean-functions head bound, is provided.

entries.title: Local Modifications of Nearest-Neighbor and Min-Plus Representations
entries.authors: Liliia Redina
entries.checked_location: Theorem 9 and its proof, and Theorem 5
entries.mechanism: A min-plus representation on the cube can correct d prescribed labels by adding d affine forms. The correction adds 2 times Hamming distance minus 1 to an existing minimizing form.
entries.gap: Evaluation uses minima of labeled affine forms, not a sum of affine fractions. The correcting forms have mixed slopes at a general vertex, and no admissible constant-head compiler is supplied. This is a local modification theorem, not a universal quadratic head saving.

entries.title: On Algebraic Constructions of Neural Networks with Small Weights
entries.authors: Kordag Mehmet Kilic, Jin Sima, and Jehoshua Bruck
entries.checked_location: Theorem 1, Lemma 2, Section IV, and the decoding appendix
entries.mechanism: A recursive ternary detecting matrix A_k = [[A_{k-1},A_{k-1},I],[A_{k-1},-A_{k-1},0]] has m_k=2^k m_0 rows and n_k=2^k(n_0+k m_0/2) columns, with no nonzero ternary kernel vector. The proof uses parity to recover the identity-block coordinates. Siegel’s lemma bounds the achievable rate.
entries.application: This supplies a concrete number-theoretic and coding-theoretic compression mechanism for integer equality tests. With m_0=n_0=1 the rate is k/2+1. It was checked as a possible address encoder for the head problem.
entries.gap: The decoder explicitly uses reduction modulo two and recursive arithmetic. The circuit consequences concern EQUALITY and COMPARISON with extra threshold/equality gates, not arbitrary Boolean tables in a flat sum of admissible affine fractions. No head compiler with the requested cost is supplied.

entries.title: Erdos-Pyber theorem for hypergraphs and secret sharing
entries.authors: Laszlo Csirmaz, Peter Ligeti, and Gabor Tardos
entries.checked_location: Theorem 2 and Lemma 1, pages 4-6
entries.mechanism: Partition vertices into short lists and group opposite vertices by their neighbourhoods on each list. This gives constructive biclique partitions with vertex load (1+o(1))v/log_2(v), and a fractional variant with constant one half.
entries.application: Motivates the separately proved small-rectangle partition in mechanism-audit.tex, which attains O(2^n/n^2) monochromatic cells.
entries.gap: Cells are not attention heads. A parity restriction disproves a uniform constant-head compiler for all logarithmic-side rectangles; exact numerical indicators need at least n-log_2(cell size) heads. An amortized compiler and flat combination mechanism remain absent.

entries.title: Approximating Boolean functions with depth-2 circuits
entries.authors: Eric Blais and Li-Yang Tan
entries.checked_location: Proposition 4.4, Theorems 4 and 14, and the covering-code discussion in Section 4
entries.mechanism: Radius-d Hamming-ball covers produce one-sided local degree-d polynomial threshold approximators. Their disjunction gives O(1/n) error using O(2^n/n^d) degree-d gates for fixed d. Radius-one asymptotically perfect covers sharpen the linear-threshold version.
entries.gap: For d=2 the number of gates has the requested order, but these are general quadratic threshold gates, the result permits errors, and it composes the gates by disjunction. None of these operations is a constant-cost flat affine-fraction construction. The local radius-two compiler is independently excluded by the previously recorded parameter count.

entries.title: Rational Parametrizations of Neural Networks
entries.authors: Uwe Helmke and Robert C. Williamson
entries.checked_location: Definitions 2.1-2.2, Corollaries 3.2-3.3, Theorems 4.4 and 5.1, and Section 6; the 1995 journal extension abstract was also inspected.
entries.mechanism: Scalar analytic networks are parametrized through matrix function realizations and proper rational functions. A Hankel rank characterizes finite realization dimension under the stated hypotheses.
entries.gap: These are scalar functional realizations, potentially with Jordan blocks and complex poles. Neither a Boolean-cube sign construction nor a bound by admissible affine input denominators follows. The realization theorem assumes a finite realization already exists and does not supply the required universal head count.

entries.title: On the representation of directed graphs as unions of orderings
entries.authors: Paul Erdos and Leo Moser
entries.checked_location: Sections 2 and 3, especially Lemmas 2 and 4 and the final bilevel-graph decomposition
entries.mechanism: Every oriented graph on m vertices is induced by O(m/log(m)) rankings. Pairs of rankings encode disjoint complete bipartite directed components and cancel elsewhere.
entries.application: The audit proves an explicit admissible fraction (R^rank(i)-R^rank(j))/(1+R^rank(i)+R^rank(j)) approximating one ranking vote on two one-hot inputs. The majority theorem then transfers to arbitrary promised rectangular sign tables.
entries.gap: One-hot ranks are independently stored coordinates. Binary encoding makes the required rank powers nonlinear tables; even the natural binary rank has a nonzero mixed difference. No affine encoder, full-cube extension, or target-cost flat compiler follows.

entries.title: Critical Set of the Master Function and Characteristic Variety of the Associated Gauss-Manin Differential Equations
entries.authors: Alexander Varchenko
entries.checked_location: Sections 2.10 and 2.11, Theorem 2.7 and Lemma 2.8; Lemma 3.6
entries.mechanism: Logarithmic master functions have rational gradient equations. Generic weights give nondegenerate critical points; unbalanced weights give isolated points counted with Milnor numbers by the arrangement complement Euler characteristic.
entries.application: At an interior stationary head score, the fixed residual defines Phi(b)=sum_x g_x log(1+b.x). Each nonzero numerator gives grad(Phi)(b_h)=0 and Hess(Phi)(b_h)u_h=0.
entries.gap: These residuals force degenerate points, so generic nondegeneracy cannot be assumed. A Hessian kernel vector does not make the Hessian zero. The paper gives no target-order count for these residuals in the admissible chamber.

entries.title: How many sorted projections determine any n points in k dimensions?
entries.authors: Christopher Gorham Lester and Raymond Hau Sørensen
entries.checked_location: Theorems 1.1 and 1.4; Sections 1.2-1.4, version 3 dated 19 November 2026
entries.mechanism: Generic directions separate finite multisets through coloured-matching graph rigidity, with O(k log n log log n) directions.
entries.application: A fixed-multiset affine denominator array is equivalently equality of projections of two coefficient multisets along directions (1,x).
entries.gap: The Boolean directions (1,x) are a prescribed nongeneric family. Generic separation is neither a construction of numerator signs nor a compressed realization theorem. No genericity assertion for these directions is used.

entries.title: New Gate, Weight and Wire Complexity Bounds for Sigmoid Neural Networks
entries.authors: Jiatu Li, Daniel Reichman, Ryan Williams, Tony Wu
entries.checked_location: Theorems 1.5, 1.7, 6.1 and 6.2; Section 6.1 proof
entries.mechanism: Strict semialgebraic feasibility yields architecture-preserving parameter bounds after exponentiating sigmoid parameters. Other constructions use additional depth.
entries.gap: The sigmoid denominator is 1+B times a product of coordinate factors, not an affine input form. Parameter bounds assume an existing representation and do not construct every truth table with the requested number of admissible heads.
entries.rechecked_2026_11_23: Re-read the stated model distinctions and principal bounds; no stronger transfer found.
entries.additional_checked_location_2026_11_23_1: Section 6.3: Lemmas 6.6 and 6.8, Corollary 6.9, and the carry-separated product construction. Lemma 4.5 and its no-poles interval approximation statement.
entries.additional_transfer_audit: The bit decoder explicitly feeds earlier decoded bits into later gates. Its growing depth is essential to that construction. A general rational approximation with no interval poles does not supply a sum of positive affine-denominator heads. No target transfer follows.

entries.title: Nondegenerate hyperplane covers of the hypercube
entries.authors: Lisa Sauermann and Zixuan Xu
entries.checked_location: Theorem 1.1, Corollary 1.2, and Section 2 proofs; version 2 dated 4 March 2026
entries.mechanism: Choose a least-covered vertex, partition coordinate supports of incident hyperplanes, and retain same-sign support pieces. The resulting subcube reduces the problem to the Alon-Furedi covering lower bound.
entries.gap: The conclusion is a lower bound for nondegenerate covers, with a bounded-coefficient edge-slicing application. It is neither an exact cover of every prescribed subset at the target order nor a construction using admissible fractions.

entries.title: Bruhat intervals that are large hypercubes
entries.authors: Jordan Ellenberg, Nicolas Libedinsky, David Plaza, Jose Simental, Geordie Williamson
entries.checked_location: Theorem 1.1 and Section 2.1 definitions of dyadically well-distributed permutations
entries.mechanism: Dyadically well-distributed permutations in S_(2^m) form a Bruhat interval isomorphic as a poset to a Boolean cube of dimension m*2^(m-1).
entries.gap: A poset cube is not an affine cube of real permutation vectors. The audit's power-sum invariant bounds the dimension of the latter by H-1 in H coordinates. No affine denominator encoder or numerator readout for arbitrary signs is supplied.

entries.title: More on additive triples of bijections
entries.authors: Sean Eberhard
entries.checked_location: Theorems 1.3 and 1.4; Section 2 Fourier decomposition
entries.mechanism: An arbitrary function into a finite abelian group satisfying the necessary total-sum constraint has asymptotically many decompositions as a sum of three bijections, with an explicit positive singular-series factor. Four summands give asymptotic uniformity.
entries.gap: Addition is in the finite group. In characteristic two it is bitwise XOR, which is not a linear readout of decoded signs. The theorem also does not encode arbitrary permutations by affine functions of binary inputs. Both the decoder and a flat admissible composition remain missing.

entries.title: On the weight and density bounds of polynomial threshold functions
entries.authors: Erhan Oztop and Minoru Asada
entries.checked_location: Theorem 2 and its proof sketch; Theorem 3 and the integer-weight construction
entries.mechanism: A universal strict polynomial sign representation with at most three quarters of the Fourier monomials, together with explicit integer-weight bounds.
entries.gap: This is a constant-factor density saving, not order 2^n/n. Fourier monomials are parity products, and grouping them into admissible heads requires a separate compiler.

entries.title: Beyond the Signs: Nonparametric Tensor Completion via Sign Series
entries.authors: Chanwoo Lee and Miaoyan Wang
entries.checked_location: Section 3.1, Definitions 1 and 2, Proposition 1, and Examples 1-5
entries.mechanism: Tensor sign-rank can be smaller than exact tensor rank; structured high-rank tensors admit low-rank threshold slices.
entries.gap: The results do not give the required rank bound for every Boolean tensor, and a rank-one tensor factor is a product rather than an affine-fraction head. Their sign convention permits zero entries on the positive side, unlike the requested strict signs.

entries.title: Handelman's hierarchy for the maximum stable set problem
entries.authors: Monique Laurent and Zhao Sun
entries.checked_location: Sections 1.1-1.2, Theorem 1, and the hypercube literal-product cone
entries.mechanism: Nonnegative combinations of products of the linear inequalities defining a polytope give Handelman positivity certificates.
entries.application: A product of positive affine cube denominators has a direct nonnegative expansion in coordinate-face indicators of codimension at most the head count; the indicator approximation obstruction uses that elementary expansion.
entries.gap: The positivity hierarchy does not enforce factorization into admissible denominators with affine residues and does not construct all strict Boolean sign tables at the target head budget.

entries.title: Computing with Almost Optimal Size Neural Networks
entries.authors: Kai-Yeung Siu, Vwani Roychowdhury, and Thomas Kailath
entries.checked_location: Definitions 1-3 and Remark 2, printed pages 21-22; Theorem 4, printed page 25
entries.mechanism: Piecewise rational approximation and threshold-degree lower bounds for bounded-weight networks computing symmetric functions with inverse-polynomial separation.
entries.gap: The bounded-weight and separation assumptions are absent from the manuscript. The construction concerns parity and related symmetric functions, and supplies neither a universal upper bound nor a one-layer affine-fraction compiler.

entries.title: Universal Approximation with Softmax Attention
entries.authors: Jerry Yao-Chieh Hu, Hude Liu, Hong-Yu Chen, Weimin Wu, and Han Liu
entries.checked_location: Theorem 3.2, Lemmas 3.2-3.3, and Section E.3 of arXiv:2504.15956v2; the final ICML 2026 abstract was cross-checked.
entries.mechanism: Interpolation points in value vectors and data-dependent query scores approximate truncated affine functions token by token. General sequence approximation adds another attention layer or a final softmax stage.
entries.gap: The manuscript reads a fixed query token and permits only a linear output. Packing all input bits into a data-bearing query, mixing tokens before attention, or adding the second selection stage changes the model. No universal head-count construction in the stipulated model follows.

entries.title: Covering the hypercube, the uncertainty principle, and an interpolation formula
entries.authors: Paata Ivanisvili, Ohad Klein, and Roman Vershynin
entries.checked_location: Theorems 4 and 6 and the proof of Lemma 11, version 2 dated 2 October 2025.
entries.mechanism: Injectivity of a weighted Boolean-lattice incidence operator excludes low-degree polynomial support inside a skew hyperplane. An explicit signed probability formula recovers top-degree coefficients from Hamming weights divisible by an even integer.
entries.gap: The interpolation theorem assumes degree at most n/m-1/2 and concerns polynomial coefficients. It supplies neither an adaptive affine-fraction sign construction for arbitrary tables nor a target-order head bound.

entries.title: On the cactus rank of cubic forms
entries.authors: Alessandra Bernardi and Kristian Ranestad
entries.checked_location: Lemma 2, Theorem 3, and the definitions of cactus, smoothable, and border rank on printed pages 3-5
entries.mechanism: Local contraction algebras give short apolar schemes, with length at most 2n+2 for cubics in n+1 variables.
entries.gap: Small scheme length does not imply a same-length limit of distinct points. The audit gives a ten-variable cubic example with local apolar length at most 20 but outside the closure of sums of 20 cubes. A real admissible fraction deformation remains required.

entries.title: A refinement on the local cactus rank algorithm
entries.authors: Alessandra Bernardi and Oriol Reig Fite
entries.checked_location: Introduction, divided-power convention in Section 1, and algorithm scope in Section 2
entries.mechanism: Constructs minimal local apolar schemes and generalized additive decompositions using multiplication and Hankel operators.
entries.gap: The algorithm does not prove a same-length real smoothing, an admissible denominator realization, or an all-Boolean-functions head bound.

entries.title: Degenerating Discriminants
entries.authors: Viktoriia Borovik and Clara Briand
entries.checked_location: Conventions, Theorems 4.8 and 4.10, and the conormal parametrization in the proof of Theorem 4.10
entries.mechanism: Deletion-contraction degenerations of reciprocal linear spaces give a dual degree formula and explicit limiting dual components.
entries.gap: The work is over the complex numbers and describes discriminants, degrees, and flat limits. It supplies neither every real sign orthant nor a real deformation with positive same-sign affine denominators. Degree or multiplicity cannot be substituted for sign coverage.

entries.title: The sum-product conjecture is false for real numbers
entries.authors: Thomas F. Bloom, Will Sawin, Carl Schildkraut, Dmitrii Zhelezov
entries.checked_location: Lemma 4.1 and its proof; Theorems 6.2 and 6.3 and their proofs; Lemmas 3.3-3.5
entries.mechanism: Multiply an additive lattice window by a logarithmic unit-lattice window in totally real fields of growing degree and bounded root discriminant. Counting produces many additive and multiplicative relations.
entries.gap: The estimates do not ensure arbitrary signatures or a matching in every orthant. Conjugate values cannot be selected freely by affine Boolean inputs; the audit proves the exact character-support condition. A trace identity counts its embeddings as separate fractions.

entries.title: Remarks on the disproof of the unit distance conjecture
entries.authors: Noga Alon, Thomas F. Bloom, W. T. Gowers, Daniel Litt, Will Sawin, Arul Shankar, Jacob Tsimerman, Victor Wang, Melanie Matchett Wood
entries.checked_location: Section 2.1, Lemmas 2.1 and 2.2 and Proposition 2.3
entries.mechanism: Many modulus-one elements in a CM field give many lattice-window pairs at a specified distance after an injective projection. Bounded root discriminant and split primes control the exponential factors.
entries.gap: Complex modulus one is not a real sign condition. Neither a prescribed Boolean encoder nor arbitrary real orthant coverage nor an admissible fraction compiler is supplied.

entries.title: Cutting towers of number fields
entries.authors: Farshid Hajir, Christian Maire, Ravi Ramakrishna
entries.checked_location: Introduction and Section 2; tower application cross-checked with Proposition 2.3 of arXiv:2605.20695v1
entries.mechanism: Refined Golod-Shafarevich inequalities permit quotienting pro-p towers while retaining infinitude, controlling ramification and imposing splitting conditions.
entries.gap: Field towers and splitting primes do not supply the required affine sign representation. No arbitrary-sign or head-count statement is inferred.

entries.title: On the extension complexity of polytopes separating subsets of the Boolean cube
entries.authors: Pavel Hrubes, Navid Talebanfard
entries.checked_location: Lemma 5, Theorem 6 and their proofs; Section 4.1
entries.mechanism: A bipartite graph on one-hot encodings of half-inputs gives a separating polytope with O(2^(n/2)) lifted inequalities. Boolean points have unique one-hot fibers under projection.
entries.gap: The auxiliary one-hot variables are not affine functions of the original bits. Eliminating the lifted variables with the desired affine-fraction cost is unproved; treating the encoding as free changes the model.

entries.title: On the Complexity of Computing a Random Boolean Function Over the Reals
entries.authors: Pavel Hrubes
entries.checked_location: Lemma 4.1, Theorem 4.2 and proofs; quantifier-elimination discussion in Section 5
entries.mechanism: A single integer stores the truth table; recursively alternating quantifiers define large integer intervals and decode its selected binary digit. Formula size O(k*2^(n/k)) uses 2k-1 quantifier blocks.
entries.gap: Attention has no quantified integer-membership operation. A fixed rational decoder of one scalar for N arbitrary signs requires N*H >= 2^N-1, so this encoding cannot be transferred by an uncharged bit-extraction step.

entries.title: Distinct permutation dot products
entries.authors: Cosmin Pohoata
entries.checked_location: Theorem 1.1 statement; Theorem 2.1 and Lemma 3.2 with proofs
entries.mechanism: Subset-sum support is bounded below by m^(2k+1)/E_k(D). Disjoint transpositions embed translates of subset sums into the values of permutation dot products.
entries.gap: Many distinct scalar outputs do not give arbitrary simultaneous sign words. The disjoint-swap output is affine in its selection bits; neither a target-dependent interacting affine permutation cube nor its required reciprocal readout is constructed.

entries.title: On the number of permutation-twisted dot products
entries.authors: Ruben Carpenter, Colin Defant, Noah Kravitz
entries.checked_location: Theorem 1.1 and Section 2 real-case proof, including Lemmas 2.1 and 2.2
entries.mechanism: Greedy disjoint pairs yield positive superadditive difference sequences. Products of those sequences have cubically many subset sums, giving an optimal-order support bound for permutation dot products.
entries.gap: The conclusion counts distinct values as a permutation varies, not labelings on the Boolean cube. Its disjoint-transposition construction leaves the scalar value affine in the swap bits. No head-count upper bound follows.

entries.title: Logarithmic asymptotics for polynomial threshold functions
entries.authors: Martin Anthony
entries.checked_location: Theorems A-D statements and Section 2.1 evaluation matrices; no claim to have audited all 39 pages.
entries.mechanism: Uniform asymptotic counting of polynomial threshold functions using Reed-Muller evaluation matrices and independent-set counts.
entries.gap: A count asymptotic to all Boolean functions is not universal realization. No conversion to the manuscript affine-fraction head budget is supplied.

entries.title: Signature of units and pseudo-units
entries.authors: Denis Simon
entries.checked_location: Introduction, Theorem 1, Proposition 6 and Section 2 proof.
entries.mechanism: The signature rank of pseudo-units equals the real degree minus the difference of narrow and ordinary class-group 2-ranks; the reflection bound yields rank at least half the real degree.
entries.gap: The signature statement is not universal surjectivity in general. Even surjectivity would not place the elements or their inverses in the affine Boolean conjugate subspace.

entries.title: Sums of values of a rational function
entries.authors: Bjorn Poonen
entries.checked_location: Theorems 1.1-1.2, introductory proof sketch, Proposition 2.1, Lemma 3.2 proof through the split-prime pole-isolation construction.
entries.mechanism: Fractional-linear substitutions, pole translations, a Laurent-module Nullstellensatz argument, and split primes isolate poles and yield bounded sums or differences over a number field.
entries.gap: Inputs and substitution coefficients range over the whole field. The manuscript permits affine Boolean numerator and denominator tables only, and the proof does not bound conversion into that restricted family.

entries.title: Waring's problem for rational functions in one variable
entries.authors: Bo-Hae Im, Michael Larsen
entries.checked_location: Section 2, Theorems 3.1-3.2, Lemma 3.4 and induction through Case 1.
entries.mechanism: Power-vector sumsets over an entire characteristic-zero field are closed under multiplication with a quantified increase in the number of summands; finite differences and induction give additive bases.
entries.gap: Multiplication and unrestricted field inputs leave the affine conjugate subspace. Existence of a field additive basis does not establish the required asymptotic head count.

entries.title: Axiomatization of the Mixed Logit Model
entries.authors: Kota Saito
entries.checked_location: Definitions 1--5, Propositions 1--2, Corollary 6 and its displayed proof, Appendix C argument for Proposition 2.
entries.mechanism: The affine hull of random utility functions contains every random choice function; grouping the positive and negative coefficients yields two mixtures. General position and polynomial utility lifting characterize interior mixed-logit representability.
entries.gap: Two mixtures do not mean two logit components. The grouping proof retains all original components and supplies no O(2^n/n^2) component bound. Arbitrary utility feature lifting also cannot be identified with affine Boolean input denominators.

entries.title: Tight Bounds for the VC-Dimension of Piecewise Polynomial Networks
entries.authors: Akito Sakurai
entries.checked_location: Theorem 4.1, Lemmas 4.2-4.7, Theorem 4.8 and its encoder-decoder proof; Theorem 5.1
entries.mechanism: Iterates of a quadratic map store and extract bits. A separate interpolation subnetwork loads codes, and the decoder uses additional layers.
entries.gap: The construction uses iterated polynomial activations and a separately computed encoder on selected input points. It does not flatten to the manuscript model, shatter its entire prescribed cube, or provide an admissible rational decoder with a charged head count.

entries.title: Edge-isoperimetric inequalities in the grid
entries.authors: Bela Bollobas and Imre Leader
entries.checked_location: Author institutional publication page and abstract, including the induced-edge upper bound; the full paper proof is not invoked.
entries.mechanism: Sharp bounds on the edges spanned by finite subsets of Cartesian grids.
entries.application: A related consecutive-coordinate-fiber graph is used in full-box-parity-obstruction.tex. Its edge bound is proved there directly by induction and the binary entropy inequality, rather than inferred from the abstract.
entries.gap: This gives an obstruction to a continuous permutation decoder, not a universal head construction.

entries.title: The Prouhet-Tarry-Escott Problem and Generalized Thue-Morse Sequences
entries.authors: Ethan D. Bolker, Carl Offner, Robert Richman, and Catalin Zara
entries.checked_location: Definitions 3.1 and 3.3, Theorem 3.7 and its proof, and Section 5 in the primary arXiv paper.
entries.mechanism: A Latin-square concatenation increases moment regularity while multiplying word length by the alphabet size.
entries.gap: An arbitrary initial word remains only as one block of an expanded word. Equal moments do not provide an affine-fraction decoder of its arbitrary labels or a compressed full-cube construction. Binary iteration multiplies length by two per gained order of regularity.

entries.title: Combinatorial and Probabilistic Formulae for Divided Symmetrization
entries.authors: Fedor V. Petrov
entries.checked_location: Section 1, printed pages 1-2, full graph divided-symmetrization definition, degree reduction, and cancellation proof.
entries.mechanism: Symmetrization of P divided by a graph product of coordinate differences is a polynomial of degree at most deg(P)-|E|.
entries.application: The explicit signed measure 1/Q_E on a fixed complete permutation orbit proves exact threshold degree |E| for graph inversion parity; see permutation-parity-degree.tex.
entries.gap: This obstructs a uniform affine-fraction decoder. It does not construct every Boolean sign table or apply to arbitrarily pruned representative sets.

entries.title: Permutohedra, Associahedra, and Beyond
entries.authors: Alexander Postnikov
entries.checked_location: Proposition 3.4 and its alternating-polynomial proof, printed page 8.
entries.mechanism: Divided symmetrization on a path vanishes below degree p-1; a Vandermonde denominator turns the symmetrized numerator into an alternating polynomial.
entries.application: Supports the self-contained graph cancellation proof in permutation-parity-degree.tex.
entries.gap: The cancellation identity supplies a decoder obstruction, not a universal admissible-head construction.

entries.title: Nearly-tight VC-dimension and Pseudodimension Bounds for Piecewise Linear Neural Networks
entries.authors: Peter L. Bartlett, Nick Harvey, Christopher Liaw, Abbas Mehrabian
entries.checked_location: Theorem 3, Remark 5, and the bit-extraction construction in Section 2.
entries.mechanism: Block bit extraction yields large shattering sets for networks with several layers. Remark 5 explicitly states that this construction gives a positive lower bound starting at eight layers.
entries.gap: An existential shattering set and a multilayer bit extractor do not give the fixed Boolean cube with one admissible attention layer. A secondary search result incorrectly suggested applying this construction directly at depth two; the primary text does not justify that transfer.

entries.title: Pattern-Avoiding Polytopes
entries.authors: Robert Davis and Bruce Sagan
entries.checked_location: Proposition 3.4 and its proof, printed pages 6-8; generators in Proposition 3.9, printed page 10.
entries.mechanism: Permutations avoiding 132 and 312 form a rectangular parallelotope with generators sum_{i=1}^j(e_i-e_{j+1}).
entries.application: Identifies the previously derived affine permutation cube as a known construction after a common shift by one. Its all-vertex permutation property is therefore not claimed as a new combinatorial theorem.
entries.gap: The polytope and Ehrhart enumeration do not provide target-dependent affine-fraction sign interpolation at the requested head count.

entries.title: Rational neural networks
entries.authors: Nicolas Boulle, Yuji Nakatsukasa, Alex Townsend
entries.checked_location: Section 2; Section 3.1, Lemma 1 and Theorem 3; Supplement A, first two pages.
entries.mechanism: Zolotarev sign functions compose type (3,2) rational units to obtain high degree with few parameters, yielding efficient ReLU approximation.
entries.gap: The construction uses depth and quadratic denominators. The manual pole argument shows that t/(t^2+c), c>0, has no finite exact real-affine-fraction expansion on an open interval. This does not exclude finite-cube sign representations or approximation. A head-efficient transfer remains unproved.

entries.title: Tight Lower Bounds on the VC-dimension of Geometric Set Systems
entries.authors: Monika Csikos, Andrey Kupavskii, Nabil H. Mustafa
entries.checked_location: Theorem 1, Lemma 3, Proposition 5 and the coordinate stretching argument in Section 3.
entries.mechanism: A specially constructed finite positive point set admits arbitrary k-box covers with size Omega(d*k*log k). Stronger stretching gives a reciprocal-sum classifier with k positive affine denominators; see gapped-cover-audit.tex.
entries.gap: The input set is existentially selected. An affine or common-denominator projective transfer from the full cube is excluded by the parity halfspace-cover obstruction. Nonlinear flat compilation is not established.

entries.title: New Lower Bounds for epsilon-Nets
entries.authors: Andrey Kupavskii, Nabil H. Mustafa, Janos Pach
entries.checked_location: Lemma 2 and Section 4, including the binary-prefix boxes and the inductive hitting-box construction in Lemma 7.
entries.mechanism: Parity-controlled local choices of dyadic boxes route 2^(k-1) hitting points through arbitrary selected subsets of d*(k+1)*2^(k-2) boxes.
entries.gap: Binary prefix routing and coordinate stretching do not give affine functions of all Boolean inputs. The exact scalar reciprocal transfer on the constructed point set is recorded separately; universal cube coverage is missing.

entries.title: Algebras generated by reciprocals of linear forms
entries.authors: Hiroaki Terao
entries.checked_location: Theorems 1.3 and 1.4; Proposition 2.2 and their proofs.
entries.mechanism: The reciprocal algebra is decomposed as a differential module; its Hilbert series is expressed by the arrangement Poincare polynomial.
entries.gap: Products and derivatives of reciprocal generators exceed the flat affine-fraction head class. An exact open-set flattening obstruction is proved in mechanism-audit.tex. No finite-cube sign-compression construction follows.

entries.title: Symbolic Listings as Computation
entries.authors: Hamilton Sawczuk and Edinah Gnang
entries.checked_location: Definition 2.1, differential-computer definitions in Section 2, and Lemma 2.14
entries.mechanism: Stores YES instances in polynomial coefficients; input-selected differential operators retrieve them. Chow decompositions concern sums of products of affine factors.
entries.gap: Coefficient retrieval is not a head operation, and low Chow rank has no proved conversion to a small sum of admissible affine fractions. No transfer to the target is claimed.

entries.title: On Partial Differential Encodings of Boolean Functions
entries.authors: Edinah K. Gnang and Rongyu Xu
entries.checked_location: Proposition 1 and Definition 2; equations (2.4), (2.5), and the input-selected derivative formula
entries.mechanism: Boolean interpolation can be written as a complex product of affine factors; differential encodings extract selected monomial coefficients.
entries.gap: The displayed universal complex product can use 2^n-1 factors. Differentiation, coefficient extraction, and complex factorization are not free operations in the manuscript model. The construction does not prove the requested bound.

entries.title: On Permutations Whose Adjacent-Sum Reciprocals Sum to One
entries.authors: Jinggao Ai, Dingsheng Hu, Junmin Yan
entries.checked_location: Theorem 1.1, Propositions 1.2, 1.4 and 1.6, and the splicing and multiplicity calculations in Section 2
entries.mechanism: An inductive permutation construction preserves one prescribed reciprocal sum using controlled denominator multiplicities and edge splicing.
entries.gap: One scalar cancellation does not prescribe independent signs on all cube vertices. A simultaneous affine encoder and a quantified admissible head decoder are not supplied.

entries.title: Multivariate lookups based on logarithmic derivatives
entries.authors: Ulrich Habock
entries.checked_location: Primary abstract and indexed primary PDF Section 3, equations (13)-(15). Direct PDF retrieval returned 403; indexed text supplied the displayed identities.
entries.mechanism: Lookup membership is certified by equality of reciprocal sums weighted by table-entry multiplicities; multilinear helper functions enable a sumcheck protocol.
entries.gap: The table, witness, and multiplicity functions need not be affine. They are additional oracles, not free head operations. The exact pole-count audit does not imply a finite-cube sign lower bound.

entries.title: Functional Lower Bounds in Algebraic Proofs: Symmetry, Lifting, and Barriers
entries.authors: Tuomas Hakoniemi, Nutan Limaye, Iddo Tzameret
entries.checked_location: Theorem 1; Section 6.2 definition of the word-indexed knapsack polynomial; Section 6.3, Claim 55. March 2024 manuscript.
entries.mechanism: Alternating sums of restrictions of reciprocal knapsack polynomials yield coefficient-space identities used in algebraic proof lower bounds.
entries.gap: The knapsack polynomial includes products of input variables, and the subset expansion has exponentially many displayed terms. Neither a flat affine-fraction compiler nor the universal sign upper bound is provided.

entries.title: Stability for Hyperplane Covers
entries.authors: Shagnik Das, Valjakas Djaljapayan, Yen-chi Roger Lin, Wei-Hsuan Yu
entries.checked_location: Definition 1, Theorem 3, Corollary 4 and Section 2; publication date November 20, 2026.
entries.mechanism: Classifies weight-one hyperplanes for the Clifton-Huang weighting and proves a 1/n gap for all other hyperplanes; applies to origin-avoiding multiplicity covers.
entries.gap: The target subset is not arbitrary. These weighted incidence results do not prove an O(2^n/n^2) exact cover of every subset or an admissible head compiler.

entries.title: Partial fraction decompositions on hyperplane arrangements
entries.authors: Claire de Korte and Teresa Yu
entries.checked_location: Equation (7), Theorems 2.5, 2.7, 5.2 and 5.3 in primary HTML and extracted PDF text. PDF screenshot failed.
entries.mechanism: Homogeneous product ideals characterize degree-controlled partial fractions via vanishing on arrangement flats.
entries.gap: The displayed affine Theorem 5.3 omits flats at infinity while retaining a coefficient-degree bound. The explicit B1=1+x+y, B2=2+x+y, f=xy example contradicts that bounded-degree conclusion. A corrected homogeneous criterion and Lean-checked algebraic obstruction are recorded in partial-fraction-degree-audit.tex. No finite-cube sign compression follows.

entries.title: Mixed MNL Models for Discrete Response
entries.authors: Daniel McFadden and Kenneth Train
entries.checked_location: Equation (1), Theorem 1 on page 451, limitations on page 452, and its Appendix proof on pages 465-466.
entries.mechanism: Approximates regular random-utility choice probabilities by mixed multinomial logit models using polynomial feature approximation and random coefficients.
entries.gap: The theorem permits a new nonlinear feature vector and does not bound the number of discrete mixture components. Neither change is free in the fixed affine-input head model. The proof supplies no O(2^n/n^2) component construction.

entries.title: Etudes on the methods of designing efficient circuits
entries.authors: Igor S. Sergeev
entries.checked_location: Author-hosted September 30, 2026 English version, extracted locally from the public author repository. Theorem 11.3 and proof, pages 128-129; Theorem 12.1 and proof, pages 137-138; opening of Chapter 13, pages 153-154.
entries.mechanism: Lovett-type exponent-set sum decompositions for polynomial arithmetic circuits, and orthogonal Boolean systems reducing multiplicative circuit complexity.
entries.gap: These constructions reuse nonlinear intermediate outputs and charge multiplication or circuit gates. Their bounds are not bounds on a single sum of affine fractions. No depth-removal construction with the required head count is present in the inspected passages.

entries.title: Fast Evaluation of Polynomials with Rational Preprocessing
entries.authors: Thomas D. Ahle and Jakob B. T. Knudsen
entries.checked_location: Primary PDF version displayed as v1: Section 2 cost model, Theorem 1, and construction outline through page 7. The entire 186-page paper and its Lean files were not audited.
entries.mechanism: Rational preprocessing gives monic degree-d polynomial evaluation using floor(d/2)+1 multiplications in characteristic zero or characteristic greater than d, with logarithmic multiplicative height.
entries.gap: Rational preprocessing of coefficients does not make the runtime circuit a sum of affine ratios. The circuit multiplies nonlinear intermediate quantities. No head-count-preserving flattening theorem follows from the inspected construction.

entries.title: From Sylvester-Gallai Configurations to Rank Bounds: Improved Black-Box Identity Test for Depth-3 Circuits
entries.authors: Nitin Saxena and C. Seshadhri
entries.checked_location: Definition 1, Theorem 5, and Section 2 proof outline in ECCC TR10-013 revision 1. The full 33-page proof is used as a cited theorem, not claimed to have been independently formalized.
entries.mechanism: Simple minimal real identities with k products of linear forms have factor span dimension less than 3*k^2. The proof combines ideal Chinese remaindering, matchings, and Sylvester-Gallai rank bounds.
entries.application: After common-factor removal, F-G=R with three nonzero fully real-split products has factor rank at most 26. This removes the generic-fiber hypothesis from a bounded-rank audit of logarithmic derivative cancellation.
entries.gap: Applies to polynomial identities, not just Boolean-cube identities. The resulting head-family obstruction for a sublinear number of bounded-rank groups is in split-product-rank-audit.tex. It does not exclude arbitrary admissible fractions or prove the target.

entries.title: The gonality theorem of Noether for hypersurfaces
entries.authors: Francesco Bastianelli, Renza Cortini, and Pietro De Poi
entries.checked_location: Lemma 2.4 and its proof on printed page 7 in arXiv v2.
entries.mechanism: At most 2r+1 distinct points satisfying the degree-r Cayley-Bacharach condition must be collinear.
entries.application: The real affine analogue, and the planarity threshold 2r+2, are proved directly in ideal-moment-rank-audit.tex using products of separating affine forms.
entries.gap: This constrains exact polynomial moment identities. It is not a theorem about arbitrary Boolean-cube-only identities and supplies no universal head upper bound.

entries.title: A Cayley-Bacharach theorem and plane configurations
entries.authors: Jake Levinson and Brooke Ullery
entries.checked_location: Definition of CB(r), Theorems 1.1 and 1.3, and Propositions 2.4-2.6 with the excision and elementary cardinality arguments, arXiv v2.
entries.mechanism: Small Cayley-Bacharach point sets lie in unions of low-dimensional linear spaces in specified proven ranges.
entries.application: Provides geometric context for the independent elementary planarity proof used to bound affine ideal Prouhet-Tarry-Escott cancellations by three denominator directions.
entries.gap: No unproved case of the general plane-configuration conjecture is used. The result excludes a proposed cancellation mechanism under explicit polynomial-identity hypotheses, not the full head model.

entries.title: Rational Designs and Prouhet-Tarry-Escott Problems
entries.authors: Ryutaro Misawa, Masanori Sawa, and Filip Spiranec
entries.checked_location: Definition 2.9, Theorem 2.10 and its proof including Lemma 2.11, Proposition 2.16 and proof, and Theorem 3.4 and proof. Other existence and optimality claims in the 56-page paper were not independently audited.
entries.mechanism: Pigeonhole arguments for character sums in number-field lattices construct disjoint equal-moment blocks. A group-action construction removes multiplicities from rational designs; a related construction represents ring elements as sums of distinct units.
entries.gap: The design replacement has cardinality m*|A1|, where m is the original sum of integer weights, and does not reduce the number of terms. The number-field units and multiplicative group actions are not automatically admissible affine fractions of the original input. No target-dependent sign construction with O(2^n/n^2) heads or quantitative transfer to that count is established.

entries.title: On the Computation of Boolean Functions by Analog Circuits of Bounded Fan-In
entries.authors: Gyorgy Turan and Farrokh Vatan
entries.checked_location: Theorem 4.1, Lemma 4.2 and their proofs on printed page 203; circuit model in Section 2.
entries.mechanism: A quadratic map with two inverse branches encodes an arbitrary bit string in one real parameter. Iteration of that map decodes the string; addressing and selection give O(2^(n/2)) arithmetic gates.
entries.gap: The decoder uses sequential nonlinear composition and products of intermediate outputs. Those operations are absent from a single affine-fraction sum. The construction does not bound head count.

entries.title: The multidimensional truncated moment problem: Caratheodory numbers
entries.authors: Philipp J. di Dio and Konrad Schmudgen
entries.checked_location: Definitions 4 and 18, Proposition 23, Theorem 25 and its proof, and Remark 28, arXiv v2.
entries.mechanism: The signed Caratheodory number is at most twice the least atom count at which the moment-map derivative has full rank. The proof uses an open image at a regular point and differences of nearby moment vectors.
entries.gap: This represents every numerical moment vector. The full-rank requirement already needs at least m/(d+1) atoms for m functions on a d-dimensional domain. It gives no additional logarithmic saving specific to strict signs, and does not bypass the exact-table dimension obstruction.

entries.title: Hadamard products of linear spaces
entries.authors: Cristiano Bocci, Enrico Carlini, and Joe Kileel
entries.checked_location: Complex-field convention in Section 2, Theorem 6.8 and proof, Remark 6.9, and Corollary 6.10 and proof, printed pages 612-614.
entries.mechanism: Tropical intersection and identifiability calculate dimension and degree of Hadamard products of generic linear spaces and reciprocal linear spaces in sufficiently high ambient dimension.
entries.gap: The Boolean affine-evaluation space is special, not generic. Componentwise products are not head sums. Complex dimension and degree alone do not ensure a real point in each strict orthant or positivity and common orientation of denominator slopes.

entries.title: Almost Linear VC Dimension Bounds for Piecewise Polynomial Networks
entries.authors: Peter L. Bartlett, Vitaly Maiorov, and Ron Meir
entries.checked_location: Introduction on printed page 191 and Theorem 3.1 with proof on pages 195-196.
entries.mechanism: Packed real parameters, sequential threshold bit extraction, and address selection give large VC dimension with increasing depth. The introduction separately distinguishes real-input two-layer results from binary-input three-layer results.
entries.gap: The decoder is a sequence of nonlinear layers. A shatterable point set is not the prescribed complete Boolean cube. Neither the decoder nor the activation transfer is a one-layer sum of admissible affine fractions.

entries.title: Tight Bounds for the VC-Dimension of Piecewise Polynomial Networks
entries.authors: Akito Sakurai
