entries.checked_location: Depth convention in Section 2; Theorem 4.1, Lemmas 4.2-4.7, Theorem 4.8 and the encoder construction; Section 5 proof outline.
entries.mechanism: Iterated quadratic maps decode real-parameter bit strings; polynomial feature products implement an encoder. Piecewise polynomial arrays replace parts of the iterated decoder.
entries.gap: The construction uses additional nonlinear layers, multiplies intermediate features, and chooses a special input set. None is a free operation in the manuscript model. No full-cube one-layer head construction is obtained.

entries.title: On the power of border of depth-3 arithmetic circuits
entries.authors: Mrinal Kumar
entries.checked_location: Model and border definition, Theorem 1.5, and Section 3.1 proof of the product construction.
entries.mechanism: For P=sum_i L_i^d, the product of 1+epsilon^d*L_i^d has P as its first nonconstant term. Splitting over the complex numbers yields top fan-in two with d*T affine factors.
entries.gap: Top fan-in is not factor count or head count. Complex factors need not be real admissible denominators. The direct replacement by a product of admissible real factors minus a constant cannot sign-represent parity in dimension at least three, as proved in border-real-factor-audit.tex. No general real transfer is established.

entries.title: Rational Functions as Sums of Reciprocals of Polynomials
entries.authors: Neil Epstein
entries.checked_location: Main theorem and its constructive existence proof by successive division, accepted author version pages 3-4.
entries.mechanism: A proper univariate rational function has a finite alternating expansion with denominators h0, h0*h1, and successive products, where the factor degrees increase strictly.
entries.gap: The displayed denominators are nonlinear polynomial products. The theorem neither makes them admissible affine forms nor bounds the cost of any conversion to heads.
entries.rechecked_2026_11_23: Read the full main theorem proof, its uniqueness argument, Proposition 3, Theorem 5, and the Euclidean-domain discussion. The nonlinear denominator-product gap remains.

entries.title: Bounding the Vapnik-Chervonenkis Dimension of Concept Classes Parameterized by Real Numbers
entries.authors: Paul W. Goldberg and Mark R. Jerrum
entries.checked_location: Theorem 2.1, printed page 137 (PDF page 6), restating Warren’s strict polynomial sign-pattern theorem.
entries.mechanism: For m degree-at-most-d real polynomials in p variables with m >= p, the number of strict sign patterns is at most (4 e d m / p)^p. Affine-weighted exponential scores on Boolean inputs become degree-at-most-n+1 polynomials in (2n+1)H+1 parameters.
entries.gap: This proves an obstruction to common-Laplace-time constructions and ideal moment variations, not a lower bound for unrestricted sums of positive affine reciprocals. Cancellation across integration times is permitted in the original model.

entries.title: On the Approximation of Stieltjes Functions by Exponential Sums and Rational Functions with Applications to Partial Differential Equations
entries.authors: Dietrich Braess and Wolfgang Hackbusch
entries.checked_location: Revised August 2026 version: Sections 1.3-1.4 and 2.2-2.3, Theorem 4.5 and its proof, and Addendum B Theorem B.1.
entries.mechanism: Approximates inverse powers on positive intervals by exponential sums; exponentials of sums factor into products. Relative-error bounds depend on the interval ratio, with improved bounds from variable-angle complex cones and Zolotarev approximation.
entries.gap: A head-by-head relative error epsilon controls a signed score only through the sufficient bound epsilon times the sum of head magnitudes. That sum relative to the margin is unrestricted and may be enormous. No uniform constant-term replacement or construction of arbitrary Boolean signs follows. The separate Boolean exponential count rules out universally preserving all signs with o(n/log n) common quadrature times at the requested head budget.
entries.scope: No lower bound on best scalar approximation length is inferred from the paper’s upper error estimates; correlated approximation errors are not assumed impossible.

entries.title: The sharp deficit in primitive signed reciprocal relations
entries.authors: Will Howe, Grant Huffman, Jensen Kohlmeyer, and Liam Kruer
entries.checked_location: Theorem 1.1; Lemmas 2.2, 3.1, 4.1 and 4.2, including the prime-path and rational-completion proofs; Proposition 4.3 and its proof. The full converse was not audited.
entries.mechanism: Connects divisor blocks by prime-indexed paths using Chinese remainder constraints, then completes a scalar reciprocal sum while avoiding marked primes.
entries.gap: The denominators are scalar integers selected for one identity. No construction makes every individual denominator affine in a common Boolean input while prescribing an arbitrary strict sign table. Rescaling a scalar relation by one common affine form gives only a proportional-denominator identity.

entries.title: Short Egyptian fractions
entries.authors: OpenAI preprint, September 25, 2026
entries.checked_location: Primary TeX obtained with git at 4eaee87548250b2682affda7d05d947c05554bae: introduction.tex, elementary.tex, divisors.tex, residues.tex, random.tex, descent.tex. Read the dense-family transfer, residue construction, shifted divisor moment, and exceptional-set recurrence. Counting and prescribed-denominator corollaries were not independently audited.
entries.mechanism: Prime-product residue distributions supply many reductions; a shifted divisor moment limits propagation of exceptional numerators. A dense set then covers every numerator by two summands, proving a scalar O(log log b) unit-fraction length bound.
entries.gap: The reduction uses ceilings, residues, selected divisors, and recursively multiplied denominators. These are not affine functions of the original Boolean input. Scalar short expansions and a dense-family argument do not imply a flat affine-fraction head construction.

entries.title: Probability: Theory and Examples, version 5
entries.authors: Rick Durrett
entries.checked_location: Section 4.3.2, printed page 226, the one-step martingale calculation for a Polya urn. No convergence theorem is used in the new head identity.
entries.mechanism: Proportional reinforcement preserves the expected share of a selected color. Applying the conditional-expectation calculation to every subset containing color zero yields a simultaneous Boolean reciprocal averaging identity.
entries.gap: The identity replaces one head by n+1 heads. A general compression or same-cost implementation of repeated branching is not obtained. Complete-layer first variations obey the separate polynomial-degree obstruction in polya-reciprocal-audit.tex.

entries.title: Rings that are Egyptian with respect to a multiplicative set
entries.authors: Neil Epstein
entries.checked_location: Definition 2.1, Proposition 2.6, Theorem 2.7, Proposition 2.10, Theorem 2.12, Example 2.13 and Lemma 2.15, including their proofs.
entries.mechanism: Unit-fraction decompositions in localizations of rings, including rings with zero divisors; a regular Jacobson-radical element gives a two-term construction, and decompositions pass through products and quotients.
entries.gap: The admissible affine denominator family is not multiplicatively closed, including modulo the Boolean ideal. For example (1+x+y)(1+2x+3y) reduces to 1+5x+7y+5xy. The Boolean coordinate ring is a finite product of fields with zero Jacobson radical. Arbitrary units or power-series denominators can already contain the full target table and are not heads; the theorems provide no affine or head-count control.

entries.title: Min-Wise Independent Permutations
entries.authors: Andrei Z. Broder, Moses Charikar, Alan M. Frieze, Michael Mitzenmacher
entries.checked_location: Theorem 1 and its divisibility proof; Theorem 3 and its basic-feasible-solution proof; Theorem 7, Corollary 1, and the full inclusion-exclusion proof in Section 3.4, printed pages 642-643.
entries.mechanism: Exact minimum probabilities force positive masses for prescribed predecessor sets. Uniform families also obey the least-common-multiple divisibility condition.
entries.application: The one-anchor inclusion-exclusion invariant yields the separated-coefficient reciprocal-averaging obstruction in permutation-reciprocal-audit.tex.
entries.gap: These are permutation-distribution constraints, not an unconditional head lower bound or a universal small-head construction.

entries.title: Martingales Defined by Reciprocals of Sums and Related Characterizations
entries.authors: Vanamamalai Seshadri and Jacek Wesolowski
entries.checked_location: Theorem 2.1, its variance-function argument, and Theorem 3.1 with the conditional-expectation proof and gamma example.
entries.mechanism: Classifies affine inverse-sum regression identities and backward martingales for four positive iid distribution families.
entries.gap: These conditional-expectation identities supply no finite affine-head atom bound or universal sign construction. The new exchange identity is independently derived from two finite Polya steps.

entries.title: Hilbert cubes meet arithmetic sets
entries.authors: Norbert Hegyvári and Péter Pál Pach
entries.checked_location: Theorem 3.2, Lemma 4.3 and its Kloosterman-sum proof; definitions of prime-field Hilbert cubes and reciprocal sumsets.
entries.mechanism: Fourier and character-sum estimates bound the dimension of a finite-field additive cube avoiding a reciprocal sumset.
entries.gap: The theorem concerns modular incidence, not real sign representations. It supplies neither affine positive-denominator heads nor a head-count-preserving conversion from modular reciprocals to real reciprocals. No universal upper bound follows.
